conditionGrammar.description: Declarative conditions evaluated identically by the TypeScript and Dart engines. A condition is exactly one of the forms below.

forms.all: {"all":[Condition, ...]} — true when every child is true (empty list is true)
forms.any: {"any":[Condition, ...]} — true when at least one child is true (empty list is false)
forms.eq: {"q":"q15","eq":"yes"} — single-choice value equals the option ID
forms.in: {"q":"q15","in":["yes","varies"]} — single-choice value is one of the option IDs
forms.eqSet: {"q":"q30","eqSet":["manual"]} — multi value contains exactly these IDs, order ignored
forms.answered: {"q":"q08","answered":true} — status is answered and value is non-empty (non-blank string, non-empty array, or object). {"answered":false} is the negation
forms.age: {"age":{"gte":18}} — age in completed years derived from q06 (keys: gte, gt, lte, lt). Unknown age (no q06, mode none, invalid date) makes every comparison false

conditionGrammar.ageDerivation: mode "age": the stated age. mode "dob": completed years on the current local date of the device. mode "none" or missing: unknown.
conditionGrammar.missingValue: A question with no saved value (skipped, deferred, not applicable or never asked) makes eq, in, includes, eqSet false and answered false. A blank value is never read as "no".

engine.applicability: A question is applicable when it is in the active route list and every branching rule whose "show" is that question evaluates true. Questions without a rule are always applicable.
engine.nextQuestion: The first applicable question, in route order, whose status is not set (answered, skipped). Deferred questions are asked again on resume.
engine.staleValues: After every saved change, re-evaluate all rules (BR-11). A question that is no longer applicable gets status not_applicable, its value leaves the active profile (history is kept), and the onHide.effects apply.
engine.emptyCommit: Continuing a multi, days or text question with no value saves status skipped.
engine.exclusive: Selecting an exclusive option clears every other selection; selecting any other option clears exclusive ones. Validate on client and server.
engine.maxSelections: When max is set, a further selection is refused until one is removed (Milo line setup.maxReached).
engine.finishLater: Opens Review with the answers so far. Unasked questions on the basic and conversation routes are stored as deferred.

valueFormats.multi: ["optionId", ...] (array of unique strings, respects max and exclusive)
valueFormats.days: ["mon", ...] weekday IDs from days[], or ["changes"] / ["none"] (exclusive options)
valueFormats.height: {"cm":172,"unit":"cm"|"ft_in"} — stored in cm, unit is the display unit
valueFormats.weight: {"kg":78.0,"unit":"kg"|"lb","isEstimate":false} — stored in kg; target_weight has no isEstimate (always false)
valueFormats.detail: Free text for an option with freeText (max 50) and the q33 custom length go in the answer detail, not the value: {"text":"..."} or {"number":21}. The value stays the option ID so branching never parses text.

basic.label: Set up the basics
basic.sub: About 2 minutes. Goal, profile and how you log.
basic.notes: q07–q10 only when applicable. q31 is deferred on this route even if manual is chosen. Every question not on this list is stored as deferred. q36 (allergies) is on the basic route because it is safety relevant.

detailed.label: Personalise in more detail
detailed.sub: Around 5 minutes. Routine, habits and support.
detailed.notes: All questions in order with the branching rules. Used by Finish setting up to resume at the next deferred question.

conversation.label: Meet Milo
conversation.notes: Order and grouping are defined by the turn groups in conversation.v1.json. Applicability still follows the branching rules. Everything not asked is stored as deferred.

review.title: Here is what I noted
review.note: Skipped answers show as Not provided and can be added any time. Nothing is calculated until you confirm.
review.rowRule: Show a row when the question is applicable on the current route or has a saved value. Tapping a row edits that question and returns to Review.

questions.text: What would you most like to work on right now?
questions.miloLine: No wrong answer here. "Help me decide" is a fine choice.

questions.text: What else would make this experience useful to you?
questions.miloLine: Pick as many as you like. I will keep your main goal first.

options.label: Feel more energetic and improve my mood
Feel more comfortable in my body

questions.text: What change would feel most meaningful in your daily life?
questions.miloLine: This stays private. I only bring it up in quiet check-ins.

options.label: Feeling healthier and having more energy
Feeling comfortable in clothes I enjoy
A personal reason I want to describe

questions.text: Which tools would you like to have close at hand?
questions.miloLine: I will put these within easy reach on your home screen.

options.label: Information about eating windows and fasting

questions.text: What name would you like us to use?
questions.miloLine: A nickname is perfect. I just want to know what to call you.

questions.text: When were you born?
questions.note: We use your age to decide which features are appropriate. You can enter your age without sharing your birthday.
questions.miloLine: {name}, your birthday stays yours. A plain age works too.
questions.miloLineNoName: Your birthday stays yours. A plain age works too.

questions.text: Which sex input should we use if you choose a calorie estimate?
questions.note: Some calorie equations use this input. You can continue with habit tracking without it.
questions.miloLine: Only used if you choose a calorie estimate. Nothing is assumed.

options.label: Do not use a sex-based estimate

questions.text: Are you pregnant or breastfeeding right now?
questions.note: Only used to keep your goal right for you. During this time we focus on meals, water and routine instead of calorie targets.
questions.miloLine: I only ask so your goal fits this stage of life.

questions.text: What height should we use for your profile?
questions.miloLine: Tap the buttons to adjust. Switch units any time.

questions.text: What is your most recent weight?
questions.note: An approximate value is okay. You can update it later.
questions.miloLine: A rough number is fine. I will not treat it as exact.

questions.text: How much movement is part of a usual week for you?
questions.miloLine: Pick whichever sounds closest to a normal week.

options.label: Frequent walking, active work or regular exercise
Physically demanding work or frequent intensive training

questions.text: Is there a weight you would like to work toward?
questions.note: Optional. It never changes your daily targets. We use it to estimate how long steady progress may take.
questions.miloLine: Not sure yet is fine. We will focus on steady habits, not a deadline.

questions.reviewLabel: Time you would like to allow
questions.text: How long would you like to allow for this?
questions.note: Only a rough wish. We show what is realistic for your numbers. Nothing here is a deadline.
questions.miloLine: No pressure. I will show you what is realistic, and you can change it any time.

options.label: No set time, steady progress is fine

questions.text: Which eating pattern is closest to yours?
questions.miloLine: This only filters ideas. It is not a medical label.

options.label: Fish but no meat or poultry

questions.text: Do you have any food allergies or intolerances?
questions.note: So your plan never leans on a food you cannot eat.
questions.miloLine: I will keep these out of every idea I give you.

questions.text: Where do most of your meals come from?
questions.miloLine: So I can suggest the right shortcuts.

options.label: It changes from week to week

questions.text: Which description fits your work or study schedule best?
questions.miloLine: No reminders get scheduled until you choose a time.

questions.text: How many times do you usually eat in a day?
questions.miloLine: So any meal ideas fit the way your day really runs.

options.label: It changes from day to day

questions.text: Do you have children, and do they live with you?
questions.miloLine: Only for household planning. Skip freely.

options.label: They live with me some of the time

questions.text: Do you tend to eat more on weekends or other days off?
questions.miloLine: No good or bad days. I just want to plan around real life.

questions.text: Which days would you like your plan to allow more flexibility?
questions.miloLine: Tap the days. Any combination works.

questions.text: How familiar are you with everyday nutrition basics?
questions.miloLine: This is not a test. It only sets how much detail I give.

options.label: I know some of the essentials
I am comfortable with detailed nutrition information

questions.text: Have you used a food or calorie diary before?
questions.miloLine: If you have, I will skip the tutorial.

options.label: No, this is new to me

questions.text: What has your experience with intermittent fasting been?
questions.miloLine: Just your experience. I will not start any plan or timer.

options.label: I have tried it and found it useful
I have tried it and did not enjoy it
I have not tried it but am curious
I would like an explanation first

questions.text: How are you feeling about making changes right now?
questions.miloLine: Any answer is okay. It helps me pick the right tone.

options.label: Confident about taking the next step

questions.text: Which parts of your routine would you like to work on first?
questions.miloLine: Up to three. These are focus areas, not daily rules.

questions.text: What tends to make these changes difficult?
questions.miloLine: So I can support you without adding pressure.

options.label: Food habits that are hard to change

questions.text: When you eat without feeling hungry, what tends to influence you?
questions.miloLine: Everyone does this sometimes. No judgement from me.

options.label: Food is nearby or easy to reach

questions.text: What would help you keep your routine manageable?
questions.miloLine: Choose what sounds helpful. Nothing gets shared with anyone.

options.label: Plan and log food before meals
Check in with someone I trust
Prepare meals and collect recipes ahead of time

questions.text: When would recording meals fit most naturally into your day?
questions.miloLine: Timing only. It does not turn on notifications.

options.label: Plan the day's meals in the morning
Review the day in the evening

questions.text: Which food-related actions would you like to try?
questions.miloLine: Up to two small things. You can edit them later.

options.label: Pause and make more intentional food choices
Include fruit and vegetables more often

questions.text: Which ways of moving more would fit your life?
questions.miloLine: Adapt these to what your body likes. Up to two.

questions.text: Which changes would you like to keep track of?
questions.miloLine: Weight is optional. There are plenty of other ways to see progress.

options.label: Health or activity records from another app

questions.text: What would help you return to your routine after a setback?
questions.miloLine: A pause never triggers guilt or louder reminders.

options.label: A quiet restart on my own

questions.text: How would you prefer to add meals?
questions.miloLine: You can always switch. Photos and estimates are reviewable before saving.

options.label: Search for foods and enter amounts

questions.text: What appeals to you about entering meals yourself?
questions.miloLine: Understood. I will not keep pushing photo logging.

options.label: I want to check the accuracy myself
I prefer not to share food photos for AI processing
I want direct control over each entry

questions.text: How much time would you like to spend on tracking on a typical day?
questions.miloLine: Small is fine. I will scale what I show you.

questions.text: Would you like to choose a personal logging challenge?
questions.miloLine: Totally optional. A missed day never erases your progress.

questions.text: Where did you first come across this app?
questions.miloLine: Last one. This is only for our own reporting.
